name: Grid reliability must not be compromised

letters.desc: Duke Energy warns that proximity-based hybrid definitions and net-contractual-rights study approaches create unstudied operating conditions that threaten bulk power system reliability.
quotes: 'Nearness' of load and generation is not a technically implementable standard, and the 'nearness' of load and generation does not determine the electrical impacts to the transmission system.

letters.desc: The Maryland PSC warns that curtailment incentives and other tools that speed load additions without matching supply growth will increase the frequency of critical system conditions, and cites the 2024 northern Virginia data center trip event as a precedent for large-scale simultaneous load loss.
quotes: if a significant amount of curtailment is incentivized and implemented such that new large loads are added to the system faster than new generation can come online, a growing number of customers would be leaning on a relatively stagnant supply of electricity. This would mean that critical system conditions could be approached more frequently and reliability would be challenged more often.

letters.desc: FERC jurisdiction without detailed local knowledge of transmission, distribution, and generation could create strains on the local transmission system, particularly if generation is insufficient to handle new large loads and rapid interconnection is pursued without adequate RTO studies.
quotes: If FERC were to assume jurisdiction over interconnection of large loads without the detailed knowledge of the local transmission, distribution, and generation facility situation, it could create strains on the local transmission system.

letters.desc: OMS cautions that connecting large loads without adequate study, resource support, or cost alignment could introduce new reliability risks and inequities across customer classes.
quotes: connecting large loads to the bulk power system without thorough study, without sufficient resource support, and without appropriate cost alignment could introduce new reliability risks and inequities across customer classes.

letters.desc: The filer identifies specific reliability risks from large load growth: inflexible loads reduce the grid's ability to withstand disturbances, demand profiles are volatile, and geographic clustering stresses local infrastructure. Failure to act risks cascading outages more severe than Winter Storm Uri.
quotes: The rapid growth of data centers, cryptocurrency mining, and industrial electrification present substantial resilience and reliability risk to the power system.
Inflexible large loads have been demonstrated to reduce the Bulk Electric Systems (BES) ability to withstand disturbances, increasing risks of cascading outages during extreme events

The power system will quickly reveal if the FERC, NERC, registered entities get it wrong through outages that are more extensive, exhibit more lengthy recovery times, and are more damaging to hard to replace power delivery equipment.

letters.desc: Unlike resource adequacy shortfalls that are resolved through financial penalties and multi-year procurement, interconnection failures manifest immediately as equipment damage, voltage collapse, and cascading outages. The filer uses this distinction to argue why probabilistic VPP credit is inappropriate for interconnection.
quotes: The consequences of interconnection study failure are not financial—they are physical equipment damage, cascading outages, and potential loss of load.

letters.org: National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners
letters.desc: NARUC warns that connecting large loads without sufficient generation capacity could threaten reliable service to existing retail customers during peak demand or extreme weather events. This concern supports the case for careful state-level oversight of interconnection decisions.
quotes: any large load interconnections without sufficient available generation capacity could threaten reliable power service to existing retail customers, as grid operators may lack the resources needed to maintain system stability during peak demand or extreme weather events
